papers.title: Data Assimilation and Sampling in Banach spaces
papers.abstract: This paper studies the problem of approximating a function $f$ in a Banach space $X$ from measurements $l_j(f)$, $j=1,\dots,m$, where the $l_j$ are linear functionals from $X^*$. Most results study this problem for classical Banach spaces $X$ such as the $L_p$ spaces, $1\le p\le \infty$, and for $K$ the unit ball of a smoothness space in $X$. Our interest in this paper is in the model classes $K=K(ε,V)$, with $ε>0$ and $V$ a finite dimensional subspace of $X$, which consists of all $f\in X$ such that $dist(f,V)_X\le ε$. These model classes, called {\it approximation sets}, arise naturally in application domains such as parametric partial differential equations, uncertainty quantification, and signal processing.   A general theory for the recovery of approximation sets in a Banach space is given. This theory includes tight a priori bounds on optimal performance, and algorithms for finding near optimal approximations. We show how the recovery problem for approximation sets is connected with well-studied concepts in Banach space theory such as liftings and the angle between spaces. Examples are given that show how this theory can be used to recover several recent results on sampling and data assimilation.

llm.relevance_to_user: 本文纯理论，未涉及仿真采样效率、约束优化或UQ的实际应用，难直接迁移至植入物或生物力学设计。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a pure mathematical theory on function recovery in Banach spaces; it does not address constrained optimization, uncertainty quantification in practical surrogates, or any biomechanical or implant design context.

summary_zh.motivation: 在Banach空间中从线性测量近似恢复函数，用于参数化PDE等问题。
summary_zh.method: 利用逼近集理论并联系Banach空间几何概念提供最优恢复算法。
summary_zh.result: 得到最优恢复误差的紧先验界并给出近最优算法。
summary_zh.validation: 通过理论示例验证方法的有效性。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a general theory for recovering functions in Banach spaces from linear measurements, motivated by applications in parametric PDEs and uncertainty quantification.
summary_en.method: The recovery problem is formulated using approximation sets and connected to Banach space concepts like liftings and angles, yielding near-optimal algorithms with tight error bounds.
summary_en.result: The theory provides tight a priori bounds and algorithms for near-optimal recovery of functions from linear measurements.
summary_en.validation: The theoretical results are illustrated through examples that recover recent findings on sampling and data assimilation.

summary_en.method: A retrospective review of revision cases using this constrained liner in high-risk patients.
summary_en.result: High failure rates were observed, predominantly due to dislocation and mechanical failure.
summary_en.validation: Validation was based on clinical follow-up and survival analysis of a patient cohort.

papers.title: Biofabrication of nanogold from the flower extracts of Lantana camara
papers.abstract: The present investigation was done to explore the potential of Lantana camara ( L. camara ) flower in the fabrication of gold nanoparticles (AuNPs). The shape and size of AuNPs have been successfully controlled by introducing small amounts of L. camara flower extract. It produced spherical nanogold of average size 10.6 ± 2.9 nm without any aggregation and showed significant photocatalytic degradation activity of the methylene blue (>62%, 10 mg/L) in the presence of solar light. In addition, the experimental approach is inexpensive, rapid and eco‐friendly for industrial scale production of nanoparticles.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate a green, low-cost method for gold nanoparticle synthesis using Lantana camara flower extract.
summary_en.method: Aqueous gold ions were reduced by L. camara flower extract to produce gold nanoparticles under controlled conditions.
summary_en.result: Spherical gold nanoparticles of average size 10.6±2.9 nm were obtained, exhibiting over 62% photocatalytic degradation of methylene blue under solar light.
summary_en.validation: Nanoparticles were characterized by UV-Vis spectroscopy, TEM, and tested for photocatalytic activity.

papers.title: Automated quantitative assessment of three-dimensional bioprinted hydrogel scaffolds using optical coherence tomography
papers.abstract: Reconstructing and quantitatively assessing the internal architecture of opaque three-dimensional (3D) bioprinted hydrogel scaffolds is difficult but vital to the improvement of 3D bioprinting techniques and to the fabrication of functional engineered tissues. In this study, swept-source optical coherence tomography was applied to acquire high-resolution images of hydrogel scaffolds. Novel 3D gelatin/alginate hydrogel scaffolds with six different representative architectures were fabricated using our 3D bioprinting system. Both the scaffold material networks and the interconnected flow channel networks were reconstructed through volume rendering and binarisation processing to provide a 3D volumetric view. An image analysis algorithm was developed based on the automatic selection of the spatially-isolated region-of-interest. Via this algorithm, the spatially-resolved morphological parameters including pore size, pore shape, strut size, surface area, porosity, and interconnectivity were quantified precisely. Fabrication defects and differences between the designed and as-produced scaffolds were clearly identified in both 2D and 3D; the locations and dimensions of each of the fabrication defects were also defined. It concludes that this method will be a key tool for non-destructive and quantitative characterization, design optimisation and fabrication refinement of 3D bioprinted hydrogel scaffolds. Furthermore, this method enables investigation into the quantitative relationship between scaffold structure and biological outcome.

summary_zh.motivation: 需要无损定量评估3D生物打印水凝胶支架的内部结构。
summary_zh.method: 使用扫频OCT获取支架图像，通过图像分析算法自动提取形态参数。
summary_zh.result: 成功量化了孔径、支柱尺寸等参数，并识别了制造缺陷。
summary_zh.validation: 对六种不同结构的3D打印凝胶支架进行成像验证。

summary_en.motivation: Non-destructive quantitative assessment of the internal architecture of 3D bioprinted hydrogel scaffolds is essential for improving fabrication quality.
summary_en.method: Swept-source optical coherence tomography combined with an automated image analysis algorithm was used to reconstruct and quantify scaffold morphological parameters.
summary_en.result: Morphological parameters including pore size, strut size, and porosity were precisely quantified, and fabrication defects were identified in 2D and 3D.
summary_en.validation: The method was validated on six different representative hydrogel scaffold architectures fabricated by 3D bioprinting.
